verdicts.title: Route all integer box stores through a shared _narrow_int helper so struct-packed widths warn too
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically on a patched work copy: all before-snippets match current source verbatim (bittype.py 578-594, int.py 7-12/598-613/789-798, aggregate_types.py 150-154); every claimed repro reproduces exactly (UInt8(300)/UInt16.value=70000/SInt16.value=40000/UInt64(2**64)/SInt32(2**31)/u+=300 each emit exactly 1 warning; boundaries 255/127/-128 stay silent, 256/128/-129 warn; UInt8(True) silent; simplefilter('error') raises); legacy pack bytes byte-identical warn on/off ('2c1170' confirmed) with 0->2 warnings on the all-struct dataclass and 1->2 on UInt8+UInt7; oracle path (_legacy.to_bytes_aggregate) independently emits the same 2 warnings and same bytes, so public path and frozen oracle stay diagnostically consistent without touching _legacy_aggregate.py; fast path still taken with warn=False and correctly bails (returns None) with warn=True; no repo module imports NarrowingConfig/_warn_narrowing from int.py (structs.py and bytemaker/__init__ import from bittype.py/structs.py), so the import rewrite breaks no caller; parity tests (plan_fastpath_test + aggregate_types_test, 204 tests) and full suite 854/854 pass with all six solutions plus float-4 applied together. Nits only: (a) the warn=True fast-path bail adds a per-call NarrowingConfig.warn read on the hot path - one attribute lookup, negligible, and the author already surfaced the design question in 'decision'; (b) the recommended warn=True byte-parity test (tests item 4) should actually be added when landing, since no existing parity test runs with warn=True.

verdicts.title: Gate SInt8/16/32/64 struct packing on the instance's int_format via a shared _StructPackedSInt base
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically: before-snippets match (int.py 694-700, 731-755; bittype.py comment); SInt8/16/32/64(0, int_format='signed_magnitude').value=-5 now yields true sign-magnitude bits (10000101 etc.) with skip_struct_packing True, while plain SInt8 keeps the struct fast path (skip False, setter resolves to StructPackedBitType.value, bits 11111011 for -5, value round-trips); bit-parity with SInt.specialize(8,'b') holds for all three formats including boundaries (-128 twos, -127 sm/ones); global SignedConfig default is still honored at construction and a mid-life global flip no longer flips an existing instance (the documented sharpening); ones_complement decode via bits works (getter path); out-of-range signed_magnitude store raises ValueError exactly like SInt7 (consistent); pickle round-trips the class and instances of both formats. Full suite 854/854 incl. plan_fastpath signed_magnitude legacy-vs-oracle parity. One caveat found and cleared: copy.deepcopy of an SInt8 instance fails, but it fails identically on PRISTINE source (pre-existing FixedLengthBitVector.__deepcopy__ bug in the bitarray backend, different file) - not a regression from this change, so the solution's 'pickle verified' claim stands (it never claimed deepcopy). Style nit: _StructPackedSInt's docstring is narrative prose in a field-list-era file; defensible for a private helper base with no attributes to list.

verdicts.title: Attribute NarrowingWarning to the first frame outside bytemaker instead of a fixed stacklevel
verdicts.issues: RESOLVED by orchestrator revision: frame walk hardened with isinstance(str) check on __name__; non-string treated as user code (stops walk). Probes verified. Original issue: The attribution itself is verified correct on the patched copy for every claimed path: scalar field store, whole-array field store, NarrowingList element store, slice write, box .value setter, UInt7 constructor, and (with narrowing-2) UInt8 constructor all report the user's file/line; exactly one warning per narrowing store and zero for in-range; exec'd code with bare globals (no __name__ key) also works, attributing to the exec'd source ('<dynamic>', line 2). BUT the frame walk crashes on an edge the fixed stacklevel could never hit: if the first non-bytemaker frame's globals carry a NON-STRING __name__ (empirically reproduced with exec(code, {'__name__': None})), `frame.f_globals.get("__name__", "").partition(...)` raises AttributeError('NoneType' object has no attribute 'partition') inside the warning path, turning the opt-in diagnostic into a crash of the user's store. The pre-fix code could not raise here, so this is a new failure mode introduced by the fix; a warning helper must never raise except via the warnings filter. One-line hardening for the revision agent: bind `name = frame.f_globals.get("__name__")` and test `isinstance(name, str) and name.partition(".")[0] == "bytemaker"` (or equivalent str coercion), plus a regression test using exec with {'__name__': None}. Secondary, accepted-risk only: sys._getframe absence is handled in prose ('risks') but not code - fine for this CPython-only repo. Everything else checks out: before-snippets verbatim (including the 3-6 import block gaining sys), structs.py call sites need no change as claimed, warning-sensitive tests in structs_test.py pass, full suite 854/854.

verdicts.title: Validate int_format at SInt construction and name the parameter and choices in the error
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically on the patched copy: before-snippet matches int.py 581-587 verbatim; SInt3/SInt8 with 'twos-complement' and '' now raise immediately with the exact promised message; the previously-silent struct-packed acceptance is closed; the 'sign_magnitude' alias claim is true (to_pyint lines 124/187 and to_bitstring line 297 accept both spellings) and normalization makes the narrowing-3 gate and == comparisons see only canonical literals (alias + sign-magnitude store verified: bits 10000101); a garbage SignedConfig.signed_int_format global surfaces at the next construction; all three canonical literals construct at packed and non-packed widths; specialize-minted classes inherit the validation. Only one repo call site passes int_format explicitly (test/bittypes_test.py:446, valid literal) - nothing breaks; full suite 854/854. The open 'decision' (drop the alias entirely per the sole-user rule) is properly surfaced for the maintainer. No issues.

verdicts.title: Re-export NarrowingConfig and NarrowingWarning from bytemaker.bittypes
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically: before-snippets match bittypes/__init__.py line 1 and the __all__ head verbatim; after the patch `from bytemaker.bittypes import NarrowingConfig, NarrowingWarning` works, both names are in __all__, star-import binds them, they are identical objects to the top-level bytemaker exports, and every name in the expanded __all__ resolves (no stale entries). No import cycle (bittype.py imports nothing from the subpackage init). Full suite 854/854 including public_api_test.py. No issues.

verdicts.title: Document the C-promotion / store-narrowing contract in the Int class and module docstrings
verdicts.issues: Docs-only change, verified on the patched copy: module docstring is set and contains 'promotion model' and 'narrowing cast'; Int.__doc__ contains the new contract paragraph; the documented semantics are all TRUE on the patched copy including the float-4 compose (UInt8(200)+UInt8(100) is plain int 300; ~, unary -, +, abs all promote to plain int; UInt8(a+b)==44 is the narrowing cast; u+=300 narrows; NarrowingConfig.warn opt-in works); no runtime behavior change; 854/854. Two concrete fixes for the revision agent: (1) the suggested smoke test `assert 'narrowing cast' in Int.__doc__` FAILS as written because the phrase wraps across a line in the class docstring ('...is the narrowing\n    cast (...'); either reflow the docstring so the phrase is unbroken (as it already is in the module docstring) or normalize whitespace in the assert - empirically confirmed. (2) Wording nit: both docstrings say 'binary operators (including ... `~`)' but `~` is a unary operator; and with float-4 accepted in the float group, unary -/+/abs also promote yet the new paragraphs only name `~` - merge the wording once as narrowing-6's own risks note anticipates. Style is consistent with the file's existing prose-intro-then-field-list pattern (UInt's docstring does the same).
